He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Rhode Island Rams men's basketball|Rhode Island Rams]]. ==High school career== Dowtin attended [[St. John's College High School|St. John's College]], where he averaged 15.3 points and five assists per game as a senior, leading the Cadets to a 29–5 record, including a 16–2 mark in the Washington Catholic Athletic Conference, and was named to the 2015–16 [[Washington Post]] All-Met Second Team while also earning All-DCSAA and All-WCAC honors. In 2016, he was identified as a three-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] by ''[[Scout.com|Scout]]'', ''[[Rivals.com|Rivals]]'', and ''[[ESPN]]'' and was ranked the #43 point guard in the nation by ''ESPN'' and the 21st-best combo guard by ''[[247Sports]]''.{{cite web|title=Jeff Dowtin – Rhode Island University Athletics|url=https://gorhody.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/jeff-dowtin/5227|website=GoRhody.com|access-date=April 9, 2021}} ==College career== Dowtin played [[college basketball]] for [[Rhode Island Rams men's basketball|Rhode Island]], where he appeared in 128 games and averaged 11 points, 2.8 rebounds, 3.7 assists, and 1 steal, while shooting 44.7% from the field and 36.1% from behind the 3-point line. Dowtin also helped lead the Rams to two NCAA tournament appearances, in 2017 and 2018.{{cite web|first=Matt|last=Evans|title=2020–21 G League Bubble Roster Preview: Lakeland Magic|url=https://nbacallups.com/2021/01/23/2020-21-g-league-bubble-roster-preview-lakeland-magic/|website=NBACallUps.com|date=January 23, 2021|access-date=April 9, 2021|archive-date=March 1, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210301041843/https://nbacallups.com/2021/01/23/2020-21-g-league-bubble-roster-preview-lakeland-magic/|url-status=dead}} As a senior, he averaged 13.9 points, 3.5 rebounds, and 3.2 assists, earning a spot in the All-[[Atlantic 10 Conference|Atlantic 10]] third team.{{cite web|first=Arthur|last=Hill|title=Magic Place Three Players On Waivers|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/jeff-dowtin|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=December 19, 2020|access-date=April 9, 2021}} ==Professional career== ===Lakeland Magic (2021)=== After going undrafted in the [[2020 NBA draft]], Dowtin signed on December 19, 2020, an [[Exhibit 10]] deal with the [[Orlando Magic]] and was waived the same day. On January 24, 2021, he signed as an affiliate player with the [[Lakeland Magic]] of the [[NBA G League]],{{cite web|title=Lakeland Magic Finalize Roster|url=https://lakeland.gleague.nba.com/news/lakeland-magic-finalize-roster/|website=NBA.com|date=January 24, 2021|access-date=April 9, 2021}} where he played 15 games and averaged 6.5 points, 1.6 rebounds and 2.5 assists in 19.8 minutes.{{cite web|title=Jeff Dowtin Player Profile|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/player/Jeff-Dowtin/Summary/89016|website=RealGM.com|access-date=April 9, 2021}} Lakeland ended up winning the G League championship against the [[Delaware Blue Coats]], with Dowtin scoring 8 points from the bench.{{cite web|first=Zach|last=DuPont|title=THE LAKELAND MAGIC WIN THE NBA G-LEAGUE CHAMPIONSHIP|url=https://www.slamonline.com/nba/the-lakeland-magic-win-the-nba-g-league-championship/|website=SLAMOnline.com|date=March 12, 2021|access-date=April 9, 2021}} ===Golden State Warriors (2021–2022)=== On September 8, 2021, Dowtin signed with the [[Orlando Magic]].{{cite web|first=Brooke|last=Brumbelow|title=Orlando Magic Sign Jeff Dowtin, Hassani Gravett and Jon Teske|url=https://www.nba.com/magic/orlando-magic-sign-jeff-dowtin-hassani-gravett-jon-teske-20210908|website=NBA.com|date=September 8, 2021|access-date=September 10, 2021}} However, he was waived at the end of training camp.{{cite web|first=Brooke|last=Brumbelow|title=Orlando Magic Waive Four Players|url=https://www.nba.com/magic/orlando-magic-waive-four-players-20211016|website=NBA.com|date=October 16, 2021|access-date=October 17, 2021}} On October 18, he was claimed off waivers by the [[Golden State Warriors]], later turning his deal into a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Santa Cruz Warriors]].{{cite web|title=Warriors Claim Jeff Dowtin Off Waivers|url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/warriors-claim-jeff-dowtin-waivers|website=NBA.com|date=October 18, 2021|access-date=October 18, 2021}} On January 2, 2022, he was waived by the Warriors.{{cite news|first=Connor|last=Letourneau|title=Warriors cut Jeff Dowtin Jr., free up two-way contract for another player|url=https://www.sfchronicle.com/sports/warriors/article/Warriors-cut-Jeff-Dowtin-Jr-free-up-two-way-16743183.php|newspaper=San Francisco Chronicle|date=January 2, 2022|access-date=January 2, 2022}} ===Milwaukee Bucks (2022)=== On January 7, 2022, Dowtin signed a 10-day contract with the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].{{cite web|title=Milwaukee Bucks Sign Jeff Dowtin To A 10-Day Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/news/milwaukee-bucks-sing-jeff-dowtin-10-day-contract|website=NBA.com|date=January 7, 2022|access-date=January 7, 2022}} On January 12, he was assigned to the [[Wisconsin Herd]] of the G League following one appearance for the Bucks. ===Orlando / Lakeland Magic (2022)=== On January 19, 2022, Dowtin was reacquired by the [[Lakeland Magic]].{{cite web|title=NBA G League Box Score|url=https://gleague.nba.com/games/20220119/LAKWIS/|website=NBA.com|date=January 19, 2022|access-date=January 19, 2022}} He was removed from the team on January 28, but was re-acquired on February 1.{{cite web|title=NBA G League Transactions|url=https://gleague.nba.com/transactions/|website=NBA.com|access-date=January 31, 2022}} On March 22, 2022, Dowtin signed a 10-day contract with the [[Orlando Magic]]{{cite web|first=Dan|last=Savage|title=Orlando Magic Sign Jeff Dowtin to 10-Day Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/magic/orlando-magic-sign-jeff-dowtin-ten-day-contract-20220322|website=NBA.com|date=March 22, 2022|access-date=March 22, 2022}} and on April 1, he was re-acquired by Lakeland.{{cite web|title=2021-22 NBA G League Transactions|url=https://gleague.nba.com/transactions/|website=NBA.com|access-date=April 1, 2022}} Dowtin joined the [[Toronto Raptors]] for the [[2022 NBA Summer League]].{{cite web|title=Toronto Raptors 2022 NBA2K23 Summer League Roster|url=https://www.nba.com/summer-league/2022/vegas/team/1610612761/raptors|website=NBA.com|access-date=July 5, 2022}} ===Toronto Raptors (2022–2023)=== On July 19, 2022, Dowtin signed a two-way contract with the [[Toronto Raptors]].{{cite web|first=M.|last=Beloso|title=RAPTORS SIGN DOWTIN JR.|url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/news/raptors-sign-dowtin-jr|website=NBA.com|date=July 19, 2022|access-date=July 21, 2022}} On July 22, 2023, he signed a standard contract with the Raptors,{{cite web|first=M.|last=Beloso|title=RAPTORS RE-SIGN DOWTIN JR. AND HARPER JR. AND ADD FREEMAN-LIBERTY|url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/news/raptors-re-sign-dowtin-jr-and-harper-jr-and-add-freeman-liberty|website=NBA.com|date=July 22, 2023|access-date=July 22, 2023}} but was waived on October 20.{{cite web|title=RAPTORS WAIVE DOWTIN JR, GUEYE AND WINSLOW|url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/news/raptors-waive-dowtin-jr-gueye-and-winslow|website=NBA.com|date=October 20, 2023|access-date=October 21, 2023}} ===Philadelphia 76ers / Delaware Blue Coats (2023–2025)=== On November 2, 2023, Dowtin joined the [[Delaware Blue Coats]]{{cite tweet|author=Delaware Blue Coats|title=Jeff Dowtin will be joining the Coats today.👀|number=1720130628992078230|user=blue_coats|date=November 2, 2023|access-date=November 10, 2023}} and on March 2, 2024, he signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].{{cite web|title=Jeff Dowtin Jr. Signed by 76ers|url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/news/jeff-dowtin-jr-signed-by-76ers|website=NBA.com|date=March 2, 2024|access-date=March 2, 2024}} On April 4, he signed a standard contract with the 76ers.{{cite web|title=Philadelphia 76ers Sign Jeff Dowtin Jr. to Standard NBA Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/news/76ers-sign-jeff-dowtin-jr-nba-contract|website=NBA.com|date=April 4, 2024|access-date=April 5, 2024}} On July 22, 2024, Dowtin signed another two-way contract with the Sixers.{{cite web|title=PHILADELPHIA 76ERS SIGN JEFF DOWTIN JR. TO TWO-WAY CONTRACT|url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/news/philadelphia-76ers-sign-jeff-dowtin-jr-to-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=July 22, 2024|access-date=July 22, 2024}} On April 9, 2025, Dowtin scored a career-high 30 points in a 122-103 victory over the [[2024–25 Washington Wizards season|Washington Wizards]].{{cite web | last=Levick | first=Noah | title=3 observations after Dowtin's career-high performance leads Sixers over Wizards | website=NBC Sports Philadelphia | date=2025-04-09 | url=https://www.nbcsportsphiladelphia.com/nba/philadelphia-76ers/3-observations-jeff-dowtin-jr-career-high-performance-leads-sixers-over-wizards-nba/659908/?amp=1 | access-date=2025-12-06}} ===Maccabi Tel Aviv (2025–2026)=== On August 5, 2025, Dowtin signed a three-year contract with [[Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C.|Maccabi Tel Aviv]] of the Israeli [[Israeli Basketball Premier League]] and the [[EuroLeague]].{{Cite web|url=https://maccabi.co.il/news.asp?id=37738&lang=en|title=Maccabi adds guard Jeff Dowtin Jr.|website=maccabi.co.il |date=August 5, 2025|language=en|access-date=August 5, 2025}} On May 12, 2026, the team agreed to part ways with Dowtin.{{cite web |title=Former NBA guard parts ways with Maccabi Tel Aviv |url=https://basketnews.com/news-247232-jeff-dowtin-parts-ways-with-maccabi-tel-aviv.html |website=basketnews.com |access-date=13 May 2026 |language=en}} ===Napoli Basket (2026–present)=== On July 19, 2026, Dowtin signed with [[Napoli Basket (2016)|Guerri Napoli]] of the Italian [[Lega Basket Serie A]] (LBA).{{Cite web|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/jeff-dowtin-joins-guerri-napoli/|title=Jeff
